![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14274391/assets/dffdfde8c206cafe12087ed8e02d14b51a22932e83003351d9476ab84109c919.png)

Which of the diagrams shown above represent subspaces of ${R}^{2}?$
question.worked_solution:
Let's analyze each diagram in turn.

- Diagram I represents a set that does not contain the origin. But every subspace must contain the origin, so Diagram I is not a subspace of ${R}^{2}.$

- Diagram II does not represent a subspace.  In this case we have that the vectors $a=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]$ and $b=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ lie inside the given subset. But 

$$
a+b=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$

is not in the subset.

- Diagram III does not represent a subspace. There are vectors  $a=[\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{2}\end{aligned}]$  in the subset for which ${a}_{1}>0$ and ${a}_{2}>0.$   But then

$$
(-1)\cdot a=[\begin{aligned}-{a}_{1} \\ -{a}_{2}\end{aligned}]
$$

lies outside the given subset.

So, the correct answer is "None".
